name: How do permitting rules in Los Angeles affect feasibility?

mainEntity.name: How do Los Angeles permitting requirements change construction feasibility assessments?
mainEntity.text: How do Los Angeles permitting requirements change construction feasibility assessments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permitting is often the difference between a project that looks good in concept and one that can actually move forward. In Los Angeles, permitting complexity can rise quickly when a property sits in a hillside area, coastal zone, historic area, fire hazard zone, or under other overlays. A feasibility assessment should identify likely approval steps early, including whether discretionary review, special reports, or plan revisions are likely. This matters because permit-driven redesign can add months and significant soft costs. The report should translate code and agency requirements into practical project impacts: how much the design may need to change, what documentation will be needed, and where the schedule risk sits. Owners should be wary of any assessment that treats permitting as a minor afterthought, since it can be one of the biggest determinants of whether a project feels feasible at all.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permitting can change feasibility by adding time, cost, and design constraints. A site may be buildable on paper but still require extra approvals, redesigns, or consultant reports because of hillside rules, overlays, historic review, fire-zone issues, or neighborhood-specific conditions.
